sentences: I buy a block of cheddar at the grocery store and check the sell-by date before putting it in my basket.
I store the cheese in the refrigerator drawer, wrapped in wax paper, because the drawer keeps a steady temperature.
I cut the wedge of Parmesan into thin strips with a knife and place the strips on a wooden board.
I grate a block of mozzarella over the pizza, then spread the shreds evenly with the back of a spoon.
I melt slices of Swiss cheese in a pan until the edges bubble and the center turns soft.
I check the rind of the Brie for white fuzz and note whether the surface is firm or yielding.
I read the label on the cheese package to see the milk source and the rennet type listed.
I open the vacuum-sealed bag of feta and pour the brine into a small bowl for later use.
I press the curds in a cheese mold with a weight and leave them to drain for several hours.
I heat a pot of milk to a specific temperature, then add culture and stir the mixture slowly.
I separate the whey from the curds by pouring the pot through a cloth-lined colander.
I salt the surface of the cheese wheel and turn it over on the shelf each day.
I age the block in a cave at fifty-five degrees and monitor the humidity with a small gauge.
I slice a piece of Gouda and place it on a cracker with a square of quince paste.
I smell the washed-rind cheese before eating it, noting the ammonia and barnyard notes from the wrapper.
I count the holes in a slice of Emmental and compare their sizes across the wedge.
I weigh the cheese on a kitchen scale to measure the portion for the evening meal.
I scrape the mold from the hard cheddar, cut away the affected area, and rewrap the remaining block.
I place the cheese in a cooler with ice packs for the picnic and close the lid tightly.
I finish the last crumb of blue cheese and write cheese on the shopping list for tomorrow.
